title: Enhancing Segmentation: A Comparative Study of Clustering Methods
authors: Lew, L. S.; Tang Weiling, C.
tldr: A comparative study of clustering methods for customer segmentation in e-marketing, using RFM analysis and evaluating performance with Silhouette Score and Davies-Bouldin Index.
problem_and_motivation: E-marketing lacks a structured consumer segmentation plan. Traditional segmentation methods fail to capture dynamic online consumer behavior. More advanced, automated methods are needed to improve segmentation accuracy and efficiency.
approach: Used two Kaggle retail datasets with RFM (Recency, Frequency, Monetary) analysis after preprocessing.
Compared K-Means, K-Means++, K-Medoids, Agglomerative, DBSCAN, Fuzzy C-Means, Mini Batch K-Means, Mean Shift, and GMM.
Evaluated clustering quality using Silhouette Score and Davies-Bouldin Index.
Applied elbow method to determine optimal number of clusters.
Predicted Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) using Random Forests and Gradient Boosting with hyperparameter tuning.
Benchmarked proposed method (K-Means++, K-Medoids) against a reference method using K-Means and K-Medoids.
findings: num: K-Means++ achieved the highest Silhouette Score of 0.5012 at K=4.
num: K-Means++ also had the lowest Davies-Bouldin Index of 0.7481 at K=4.
num: Gradient Boosting after tuning yielded an R-squared of 0.9999 for Dataset 1 with K-Means++.
num: Gradient Boosting after tuning yielded an R-squared of 0.9999 for Dataset 2 with K-Means++.
K-Means++ demonstrated superior segmentation accuracy and outperformed other methods.
Method 2 (proposed) using K-Medoids outperformed Method 1 with higher Silhouette Scores and lower Davies-Bouldin Index.
GMM performed poorly with a Silhouette Score of 0.0452 and a high Davies-Bouldin Index of 2.6394.
Mean Shift performed reasonably with a Silhouette Score of 0.4027 and a Davies-Bouldin Index of 1.3553.
K-Medoids performed reasonably with a Silhouette Score of 0.3894 and a Davies-Bouldin Index of 0.9561.
Hyperparameter tuning significantly improved Gradient Boosting performance for CLV prediction.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper contributes to the field of customer segmentation by providing a systematic comparison of nine clustering methods, including K-Means++, and assessing their performance using multiple metrics. It demonstrates that K-Means++ yields superior segmentation accuracy and cluster quality compared to traditional methods. The study also contributes a methodological framework that integrates RFM analysis, outlier removal, normalization, and CLV prediction, offering a structured approach for customer analytics. The comparison with a benchmark paper highlights the value of incorporating additional clustering techniques and evaluation metrics for more comprehensive analysis.
directly_justifies: K-Means++ achieved a higher Silhouette Score (0.5012) and lower Davies-Bouldin Index (0.7481) compared to other methods.
Gradient Boosting with hyperparameter tuning outperformed Random Forests for CLV prediction.
Method 2 using K-Medoids outperformed Method 1 with higher Silhouette Scores and lower Davies-Bouldin Index.
GMM performed poorly with a Silhouette Score of 0.0452, indicating weak clustering performance.
The proposed framework combines data preparation, RFM analysis, and CLV prediction for robust customer analytics.
limits: The study focuses solely on K-Means, K-Means++, K-Medoids, GMM, and Mean Shift, limiting exploration of other techniques.
Scalability issues may arise when applying GMM and Mean Shift to large, high-dimensional datasets.
Clustering quality for K-Means and K-Means++ can be sensitive to initial cluster centroid selection.
Data preprocessing quality is critical; inaccurate handling can lead to suboptimal results.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: A systematic scan across all topic domains was conducted to identify relevant topics. The domains of predictive modeling (6.A, 6.B) and algorithmic evaluation (12.A, 12.B) were flagged as high relevance due to the paper's direct focus on CLV prediction and clustering method comparison. The expense categorization domain (3.A) was marked medium for its use of RFM analysis. Topics related to budget recommendation (7.A, 7.B) were considered contextual or low because while the paper's findings could inform budgeting, it does not explicitly address budget allocation. Anomaly detection topics (8.A, 8.B) were marked low due to the limited use of IQR for outlier removal. The overall topical coverage is centered on algorithmic evaluation and predictive modeling for customer segmentation and CLV prediction.

limitations: Focus was solely on K-Means, K-Means++, K-Medoids, GMM, and Mean Shift clustering methods. [unacknowledged]

remember_this: K-Means++ with 4 clusters achieved the best Silhouette Score of 0.5012.
Gradient Boosting after tuning achieved near-perfect R-squared (0.9999) for CLV prediction.
K-Means++ demonstrated greater stability and performance compared to standard K-Means.
The study provides a comprehensive framework for customer segmentation and CLV prediction.
No single clustering method universally outperforms all others, and evaluation metrics guide selection.
